resources.string: Tap a point to name its color · pinch or double-tap to zoom
Settings: color vision profile and language
Live camera with the areas you perceive differently
ColorGap uses the camera to show, live, the areas you perceive differently. Images are analyzed on your phone and never leave it.
No camera available. You can still analyze photos from the gallery.
The camera is not sending images. Close other apps that may be using it and tap Retry.
Frames arrive (%1$d) but none could be analyzed. Tap Retry or switch engine.
Camera error (code %1$d). Close other apps that may be using the camera and tap Retry.
ColorGap shows you, live, the areas you see differently from people with typical color vision. To start, tell it about your color vision.
The most common. Reds, greens, browns and olive greens get mixed up.
Reds look darker and get mixed up with greens and browns.
Rare. Blues and greens, yellows and pinks get mixed up.
Not sure? Start with Deutan 100%: it is the most frequent. You can change it anytime in Settings.
Everything stays on your phone: no image or data is ever sent anywhere.
Also highlight colors you see differently
When off, only edges that disappear for you are shown: two neighbouring colors you cannot tell apart.
Finer and faster analysis. Turn off to use the CPU.
The GPU analysis is not available on this phone: the CPU is used.

ColorGap simulates your color vision (Machado et al. 2009 model) and compares it with typical vision using the CIEDE2000 color difference. Blue areas: the color looks different to you. Yellow areas: the edge between two colors disappears for you, so you cannot tell them apart. Tap a point to see the name of its real color.
Here the edge between two colors disappears for you
Tap the colors to see them full screen.
For typical vision these two colors differ by ΔE %1$.1f: %2$s.

The number is drawn with this color on a background of its "twin", %1$s: for typical vision they differ by ΔE %2$.0f, for your profile only by ΔE %3$.1f. Dots vary in brightness, so only color can reveal the number.

People with typical vision read the number on the real plate. If you can read it too, your color vision is milder than the %1$s profile: try a lower severity, and the highlighted areas will shrink accordingly.
With your profile, no clearly different color is confused with this one, so there is nothing to hide in a plate: you tell this color apart well.
Find my severity with the number test

You will see about 20 dot plates. Each hides a number, or not: answer with the number you see, or "I don\'t see a number". The plates adapt to your answers and at the end the app proposes the color vision profile that matches them.

For a reliable result: screen brightness high, night mode and blue-light filter off, no colored sunglasses, look at the screen straight on. Don\'t guess: if you are not sure, choose "I don\'t see a number".
An estimate, not a medical diagnosis: screens and lighting change how colors are shown.
Dot plate that may hide a number
This is the profile whose simulated eye answers the plates most like you did. With it, the app highlights what you really perceive differently.
The plates could not tell for sure whether it is deutan or protan: at this severity the two are very similar, so the highlighted areas change little either way.
You read all the plates: your color vision looks typical, or milder than this test can measure (below about 40%%). You can keep the current profile or set a low severity by hand.
You missed plates that everyone can read (the number is only lighter or darker): the answers are not reliable. Check brightness and filters and try again, without guessing.
You see this color like everyone else
This color looks a little different to you (ΔE %1$.0f)
This color looks different to you: for typical vision the difference is clear (ΔE %1$.0f)
If the two squares look the same to you, that is exactly what the app measures: someone with typical vision tells them apart at a glance. Show this screen to someone next to you to compare.
Only lost edges are highlighted: colors you see differently are not.
People with typical vision see it %1$s here.
Stripes: here others see the colors differently from you. Tap an area to find out how.
